native.name: numpy
native.role: arrays, sample variance, and the FFT
native.why: bkde's FFT is R, and numpy.fft matches that role. This is the array library for later packages too. pracma conv and ifft use that FFT, and std_err uses the sample variance. Checked against pracma 2.4.6. modelr uses that variance, the type-7 quantile, and the median. Its bootstrap and permutation draws use numpy.random; the check is the partition, not R's sample. data.table stores columns as arrays. Checked against data.table 1.18.6.1. corpcor uses it for the shrinkage covariance, the symmetric eigendecomposition, and the economy SVD. Checked against corpcor 1.6.10. numDeriv stores the Richardson table as an array. Checked against numDeriv 2016.8-1.1. FNN stores points as arrays. The kd-tree and the brute scan use those arrays, and digamma of a positive integer is -euler_gamma plus the harmonic number. Checked against FNN 1.1.4.1. polynom's roots are eigenvalues of the companion matrix, and poly.orth uses the QR of the Vandermonde. Checked against polynom 1.4-1. rootSolve stores the gradient and the Jacobian as arrays. Checked against rootSolve 1.8.2.4. cluster stores the daisy rows as an array, and the mean absolute deviation is the mean of absolute deviations from the mean. Checked against cluster 2.1.8.3. randomForest fills missing entries with the median and scales the outlier score by the median absolute deviation times 1.4826. Checked against randomForest 4.7-1.2. BB stores the parameter vector as an array, and quadprog stores D, the constraint matrix, and the solution as arrays. Checked against BB 2026.1.0 and quadprog 1.5-8. slam stores triplet indexes and values as arrays. Checked against slam 0.1-56. slider stores each window summary in a fanout-16 segment tree and accumulates the sum in long double. Checked against slider 0.3.3. fracdiff's fractional difference is the FFT convolution, and the periodogram regression is a least-squares fit. Checked against fracdiff 1.5-4. lmtest stores the regressors as arrays. The Durbin-Watson matrix eigenvalues are the largest n-k. Checked against lmtest 0.9-40. urca's Dickey-Fuller, KPSS, and Phillips-Perron regressions are least squares. Checked against urca 1.3-4. ucminf stores the packed inverse Hessian as an array. Checked against ucminf 1.2.3. warp stores each distance and each boundary column as an array. Checked against warp 0.2.3. vars stores the series, the lag design, and the coefficient rows as arrays. The Johansen moment matrices are arrays too. Checked against vars 1.6-1 and urca 1.3-4. tseries stores the regression design as an array. The White scores are the economy SVD, and the surrogate inverse FFT is the length times ifft because R's inverse transform is unnormalized. Checked against tseries 0.10-63. ordinal stores the link densities and the control numbers as arrays. Checked against ordinal 2026.7-26. MASS ginv, Null, kde2d, and bandwidth.nrd store matrices and samples as arrays. Checked against MASS 7.3-66. mvtnorm stores the packed lower triangles, the correlation, and the draws as arrays. The symmetric square root is the eigendecomposition with the values reversed to decreasing order. Checked against mvtnorm 1.4-2. survival stores the response and the Wald matrix as arrays. Checked against survival 3.8-12. changepoint stores the series and the PELT cost sums as arrays, and a regression segment uses the least-squares solver. Checked against changepoint 2.3. nnet stores the design and the Hessian as arrays. Checked against nnet 7.3-21. randomForest stores the votes, the proximity, and the importance columns as arrays. Checked against randomForest 4.7-1.2.

native.name: matplotlib
native.role: figures that can be drawn in a few lines
native.why: A chart Matplotlib can draw in one to three lines is called directly. A chart function Matplotlib does not have is added once in killplot. pracma draws ezplot, fplot, polar, quiver, and the other Matlab-style charts with it. Checked against pracma 2.4.6. pwr draws the sample-size power curve with a line, points, and a vertical mark. Checked against pwr 1.3-0. polynom draws one polynomial curve and a dashed grid. Checked against polynom 1.4-1. vars draws the forecast fan through killplot.fan, which fills one polygon per interval. Checked against vars 1.6-1. tseries draws the open-high-low-close bars with vlines and hlines, and seqplot.ts with two line calls. Checked against tseries 0.10-63. xts draws the series as a line on the index and data limits. Checked against xts 0.14.3. rootSolve draws a steady1D profile as a line and a steady2D or steady3D field with imshow. Checked against rootSolve 1.8.2.4. changepoint draws the series, the fitted step, and the penalty diagnostic with a line plot. Checked against changepoint 2.3. lattice draws the trellis panels with it. Checked against lattice 0.23-1.

native.name: json
native.role: JSON tokens for jsonlite and RJSONIO
native.why: The Python standard library parses and emits objects, arrays, strings, numbers, true, false, and null. jsonlite's data-frame, factor, date, and NA mapping stays a port of the R methods. Checked against jsonlite 2.0.0. RJSONIO strips comments and turns an empty array slot into null before that parser, and the type mapping stays a port of the R methods. Checked against RJSONIO 2.0.5.

native.name: base64
native.role: base64 and base64url for jsonlite
native.why: The Python standard library encodes and decodes RFC 4648 base64. The URL form uses - and _ and drops the padding. Checked against jsonlite 2.0.0.

native.name: gzip
native.role: gzipped JSON for jsonlite
native.why: The Python standard library gzips and gunzips. A gzip header stores a timestamp, so the check is the JSON after gunzip. Checked against jsonlite 2.0.0. readr uses the same module for RDS written with compress gz, and the check is the serialization after gunzip. tools::checkRdaFiles reads a gzip rda through it and reports version 3. Checked against tools 4.5.0.

native.name: pickle
native.role: filesystem cache values for memoise
native.why: cache_filesystem stores each result in a file and reads it back. pickle is the standard-library form of that. The check is the value read back. Checked against memoise 2.0.1.

native.name: urllib
native.role: S3 and Cloud Storage requests for memoise
native.why: cache_s3 and cache_gcs store a serialized value with the same HTTP paths the R clients use. The check reads the value back from a local stand-in. Checked against memoise 2.0.1.

native.name: hashlib
native.role: MD5 and SHA-256 digests for tools
native.why: The Python standard library's hex digest matches tools::md5sum and tools::sha256sum, including a raw vector. A missing file stays NA. Checked against tools 4.5.0.

native.name: signal
native.role: POSIX signal numbers for tools
native.why: The Python standard library exposes the host signal numbers. They match the SIG* constants tools exports, and os.kill is pskill. Checked against tools 4.5.0.

native.name: pyyaml
native.role: YAML 1.1 parser for the R package yaml
native.why: CRAN yaml is libyaml. PyYAML is the Python binding of that parser, so yes, no, and octal integers stay YAML 1.1. The Python package is r_yaml because PyYAML already owns the import name yaml. as.yaml's quoting and yes/no logicals stay a port of the R emitter.

native.name: regex
native.role: Unicode grapheme clusters for cli
native.why: cli splits text with its own grapheme breaker. The regex module's \X matched those clusters, including ZWJ emoji and flags. Display width still uses cli's charwidth table, because wcwidth does not. Checked against cli 3.6.6.

native.name: subprocess
native.role: process execution for the R package sys
native.why: sys starts a program, pipes its output, and reports the wait status. subprocess is the Python standard library for that. windows_quote stays a port of the libuv rules, and a signalled child is the signal number while exit 1 is 256. Checked against sys 3.4.3. tools::Rcmd runs R CMD through it, and tools::Rdiff runs diff -bw through it. Checked against tools 4.5.0.

native.name: getpass
native.role: password prompt for askpass
native.why: askpass reads a password without echoing it. getpass is the Python standard library for that prompt. A non-interactive session returns None, matching R. Checked against askpass 1.2.1.

native.name: termios
native.role: terminal echo for askpass
native.why: askpass turns echo off with stty before readline. termios is the Python standard library for that terminal flag, and it restores the previous settings when the prompt returns. Checked against askpass 1.2.1.

native.name: subprocess
native.role: the Windows and macOS askpass dialog
native.why: On those platforms askpass runs the bundled helper through r_sys.exec_internal. That uses subprocess and keeps the helper's stdout. Checked against askpass 1.2.1.

native.name: PyICU
native.role: ICU regex, collation, break iteration, case mapping, and transliteration for stringi
native.why: stringi 1.8.9 links to system ICU 76.1. PyICU imports as icu and calls that same library, so search, collation, and boundaries match the installed package. The regex module stays the grapheme splitter for cli. stockSymbols sorts with that collator, which is R's order() for en_US. Checked against TTR 0.24.4.

native.name: scipy
native.role: cdfs and densities for extraDistr, nortest, pwr, and moments, the quantile regression linear program for quantreg, and the univariate margins for mvtnorm, and the banded solve and LSODA for rootSolve
native.why: extraDistr calls R's qnorm, pbeta, pgamma, pt, ppois, pbinom, and besselI. SciPy 1.18 matches those R 4.5 values inside 1e-15. pnorm stays math.erf. Random draws stay on boot's Mersenne-Twister, not SciPy's generator. truncnorm's mean uses SciPy's normal log cdf, which stays finite where log(erf) underflows. Checked against truncnorm 1.0-9. quantreg's Barrodale-Roberts point estimate is the quantile regression linear program, and scipy.optimize.linprog with HiGHS matches rq.fit.br coefficients, residuals, and the dual (equality multiplier plus tau). Checked against quantreg 6.1. nortest calls log_ndtr, qnorm, and pchisq. Checked against nortest 1.0-4. pwr uses qnorm, qt, pt with a noncentrality, qf, pf with a noncentrality, qchisq, and pchisq with a noncentrality. pnorm stays erfc. Checked against pwr 1.3-0. moments::jarque.test uses the chi-square cdf with 2 degrees of freedom. The normal tail stays erfc. Checked against moments 0.14.1. fracdiff's confidence interval uses the normal quantile. Checked against fracdiff 1.5-4. lmtest's F, chi-square, and t tails use SciPy. The Cox normal tail stays math.erf. Checked against lmtest 0.9-40. urca's pivoted Cholesky is scipy.linalg.lapack.dpstrf. Checked against urca 1.3-4. vars uses the chi-square and F tails, the normal quantile for forecast intervals, and the column-pivoted QR for the Granger covariance. Checked against vars 1.6-1. tseries uses the chi-square tail for Jarque-Bera, White, and Teraesvirta, and the F tail for the F form of those tests. pnorm stays math.erf. Checked against tseries 0.10-63. ordinal's log-gamma cdf and density use the gamma cdf, the normal cdf, and the log-gamma function. Checked against ordinal 2026.7-26. mvtnorm uses qnorm, pt, qt, the noncentral t, the chi-square quantile, and the Cauchy cdf for the Genz–Bretz margins and the equicoordinate quantiles. pnorm stays math.erf. Checked against mvtnorm 1.4-2. rootSolve's banded Newton step is scipy.linalg.solve_banded, and runsteady integrates with LSODA until the mean absolute derivative crosses stol. Checked against rootSolve 1.8.2.4. randomForest's classical scaling of the proximity uses the symmetric eigensolver eigen() calls. Checked against randomForest 4.7-1.2.

native.name: fcntl
native.role: POSIX record locks for filelock
native.why: filelock places fcntl locks on an open descriptor. Python's fcntl.lockf is that call. Rust File::lock is flock, and flock does not contend with fcntl, so it is not used. Checked against filelock 1.0.3.

native.name: zoneinfo
native.role: system zoneinfo for timechange
native.why: timechange reads the same zoneinfo files CCTZ reads, through the Python standard library. Fold 0 and fold 1 are the two civil times in a repeated hour. A skipped civil time is the pair of offsets around the gap. Checked against timechange 0.4.0. readr uses the same database for locale time zones and datetime offsets. tseries uses it for irregular-series weekdays and seconds after midnight. GMT and UTC are timezone.utc. Checked against tseries 0.10-63.

native.name: ctypes
native.role: system libxml2 for xml2
native.why: xml2 1.6.0 links libxml2 2.9.14. ctypes calls that library, so parser flags, XPath, schema checks, and URL functions match the installed package. The lxml wheel bundles libxml2 2.14, and building lxml needs libxslt headers this machine does not have. Checked against xml2 1.6.0. XML parses, queries, and serializes with that same libxml2. A document dump passes a NULL encoding. Checked against XML 3.99-0.25.

native.name: urllib
native.role: URL downloads for xml2
native.why: download_xml reads a URL into a file. urllib is the Python standard library for that request. A curl handle is accepted and unused. Checked against xml2 1.6.0.

native.name: urllib
native.role: NASDAQ and Yahoo downloads for TTR
native.why: stockSymbols and getYahooData read those sites. urllib is the standard-library transfer. xts is not in the registry, and zoo is already in translation, so the indicators stay on numeric arrays. Checked against TTR 0.24.4.

native.name: nlopt
native.role: NLopt algorithms for nloptr
native.why: nloptr 2.2.1 builds NLopt 2.10.0 and calls it from C. The Python package nlopt 2.10.0 is that library, so the same algorithm and stopping test return the same point. Finite differences and the option list stay a port of the R wrappers. Checked against nloptr 2.2.1.

native.name: libcurl
native.role: URL, options, and fetches for the R package curl
native.why: curl links libcurl 8.14.1. ctypes calls libcurl.so.4. The libcurl headers are not installed, so a Rust curl crate cannot be built. Escape, the URL parser, option ids, and file fetches match the installed package. Checked against curl 6.2.1 linked to libcurl 8.14.1.

native.name: openssl
native.role: AES, RSA, Ed25519, and X25519 for the R package openssl
native.why: The Rust crate opensslport calls libssl 3.5.7, the same library the R package links. AES-CTR, AES-CBC, and AES-GCM ciphertext match. The R package does not store the GCM tag, so decrypt keeps the updated bytes. Keccak uses EVP_Q_digest. MD4 needs the legacy provider. An RSA key is random, so the check is the DER byte 0x30. Ed25519 signs in one shot on OpenSSL 3, and a fixed seed matches R. X25519 agreement matches R. fips_mode and openssl_config read libcrypto. SHA-2, SHA-3, BLAKE2, and RIPEMD-160 stay in hashlib. Base64 and bignums stay in the standard library. Certificates, PKCS, and PEM are not ported further; they use the Python cryptography package. Checked against openssl 2.4.2.

native.name: socket
native.role: hostname lookup for the R package curl
native.why: nslookup resolves a hostname with getaddrinfo and keeps the first address of each family. The check is localhost, which is ::1 and 127.0.0.1. Checked against curl 6.2.1.

native.name: os
native.role: uname and os-release for utils
native.why: osVersion reads uname and /etc/os-release. os.uname and that file return the same string R stores. Checked against utils 4.5.0.

native.name: zlib
native.role: zlib lazy-load records for utils
native.why: R compression code 3 can store a record whose type byte is 1. That payload is zlib, not gzip. zlib is the Python standard library for that stream. The datasets shipped with R use type Z, and that path is the one checked.

native.name: bz2
native.role: bzip2 RDS for readr
native.why: readr write_rds compress bz2 and read_rds open a bzip2 stream. bz2 is the Python standard library for that. The check is the data frame after the stream is opened. Checked against readr 2.2.0.

native.name: lzma
native.role: xz RDS for readr
native.why: readr write_rds compress xz and read_rds open an xz stream. lzma is the Python standard library for that. The check is the data frame after the stream is opened. Checked against readr 2.2.0. utils::data reads datasets lazy-load records whose type byte is Z: raw LZMA2 at preset 6, after a 4-byte uncompressed length. Checked against utils 4.5.0.

native.name: geos
native.role: polygon and cell geometry for exactextractr
native.why: exactextractr 0.10.1 links GEOS (>= 3.5.0). ctypes calls libgeos_c.so.1, GEOS 3.13.1, for WKT, prepared contains, and coordinate sequences. The cell-coverage walk stays a port of the C++. raster, sf, and terra are not opened. A grid is an extent and a resolution, and a polygon is WKT. Checked against exactextractr 0.10.1.

native.name: csv
native.role: delimited tables for zoo
native.why: read.zoo and the read.table wrappers split fields with the Python standard library. A comma decimal and a semicolon or tab stay in the reader. The check is the date index and the two numeric columns. Checked against zoo 1.9-1.

native.name: zoneinfo
native.role: IANA time zones for warp
native.why: A POSIXct year, month, or day is the civil date in the vector's time zone. The default origin in that zone is local midnight at the epoch, read from the zone's offset. zoneinfo is the Python standard library for those IANA zones. Hour and finer stay groups of absolute seconds. Checked against warp 0.2.3.

native.name: colorsys
native.role: HSV colors for e1071
native.why: hsv_palette builds R hsv() colors. colorsys is the Python standard library for that conversion, and the hex colors match. Checked against e1071 1.7-17.

native.name: re
native.role: cell references for readxl
native.why: A1 and R1C1 ranges are matched with the Python standard library. The check is the upper-left and lower-right corners. Checked against readxl 1.5.0.1.

native.name: zipfile
native.role: xlsx package parts for readxl
native.why: An xlsx file is a zip archive. zipfile is the Python standard library that reads those parts. The check is the sheet names and the cells. Checked against readxl 1.5.0.1.

native.name: xml.etree
native.role: spreadsheet XML for readxl
native.why: Worksheet, workbook, and shared-string XML are parsed with the Python standard library. Namespace prefixes are ignored, matching RapidXML strip-namespaces. Checked against readxl 1.5.0.1.

native.name: rayon
native.role: parallel loops in place of foreach, iterators, and doParallel
native.why: Those packages are not ported. A parallel loop is Rayon. Rayon does not reproduce the R functions, and this entry is not a check.

native.name: polars
native.role: data frames in place of dplyr, tidyr, tibble, tidyselect, reshape2, data.table, plyr, and readxl
native.why: Those packages are not ported. A data frame is a Polars frame. An Excel sheet is Polars read_excel, which calls the Rust calamine reader. readxl's C++ cell API is not ported. Polars does not reproduce the R functions, and this entry is not a check.

native.name: dash
native.role: dashboards in place of shiny, htmltools, and shinyjs
native.why: Shiny's application framework is not ported. Dash is the dashboard library chosen for that job. shinyjs show, hide, and delay are a Dash clientside callback or ordinary browser JavaScript. A Dash callback is not a Shiny reactive, and this entry is not a check against shiny.

native.name: requests
native.role: HTTP in place of curl, httr, and httr2
native.why: Those clients are not ported further. A request uses the requests library. URL helpers already checked stay. requests does not reproduce a libcurl handle, and this entry is not a check.

native.name: plotly
native.role: interactive charts in place of the R package plotly
native.why: The R plotly API is not ported. An interactive chart uses the Python Plotly package, which drives the same plotly.js. A static chart stays Matplotlib. This entry is not a check against the R package.

native.name: cryptography
native.role: certificates, PKCS, and PEM in place of the rest of the R package openssl
native.why: The remaining R wrappers are not ported. Certificates, PKCS#7, PKCS#12, PEM, and the remaining signatures use the Python cryptography package, which links the same OpenSSL. Hashes stay in hashlib. AES, RSA, Ed25519, and X25519 stay in the opensslport crate. This entry is not a check against the R package.

native.name: libxml2
native.role: XML and HTML in place of the rest of the R package XML
native.why: The rest of the R package XML is not ported. A document uses the system libxml2 through ctypes, the same library the finished xml2 package already calls. lxml is not used: its wheel ships another libxml2, and building it needs libxslt headers this machine does not have. Checked XML functions stay. This entry is not a check against the rest of XML.

native.name: rasterio
native.role: raster grids in place of terra and raster
native.why: Those packages are not ported. A raster grid is read and written with rasterio. rasterio does not reproduce terra or raster, and this entry is not a check.

native.name: quarto
native.role: documents in place of rmarkdown
native.why: The document engine is not ported. Quarto renders the report. Quarto does not reproduce rmarkdown, and this entry is not a check.

native.name: sqlalchemy
native.role: database connections in place of DBI
native.why: The database interface is not ported. A connection is SQLAlchemy. SQLAlchemy does not reproduce DBI, and this entry is not a check.

native.name: tkinter
native.role: Tcl/Tk progress window for progressr
native.why: handler_tkprogressbar opens a ttk progress bar. tkinter is the Python standard library for Tcl/Tk. The check is the window title, the label, the percent, and the size, and clear TRUE destroys the window. Checked against progressr 1.0.0.

native.name: formulaic
native.role: R-style formulas and design matrices for survreg
native.why: R terms, model.frame, and model.matrix are not ported. formulaic parses the ~ formula and builds the design matrix that survreg and survreg.fit need. Agreed by the owner. Each function that uses it is checked against R on its own proof.

native.name: psutil
native.role: process information (ps)
native.why: Stand-in for the ps package: process listing, status, memory, children, and signals. Agreed by the user.

native.name: PyYAML
native.role: YAML reading and writing (yaml)
native.why: Stand-in for the yaml package: load and dump of YAML documents. Agreed by the user.

native.name: rich
native.role: terminal UI (cli)
native.why: Stand-in for the cli package: styled terminal output, rules, and progress. Agreed by the user as the mature Python alternative to cli.

native.name: libsass
native.role: C++ Sass compiler, wrapped from a Rust crate for sass
native.why: The R sass package only wraps libsass; per the wrapping rule we wrap the C++ system instead of rebuilding it.

native.name: pyarrow
native.role: Apache Arrow for arrow (wraps the Arrow C++ system)
native.why: The R arrow package wraps Arrow C++. pyarrow is the Python binding to the same system.

native.name: openpyxl
native.role: Excel reading and writing for openxlsx
native.why: openxlsx is an Excel reader and writer; openpyxl covers the same role in Python.

native.name: xlsxwriter
native.role: Excel writing for writexl
native.why: writexl writes Excel files; xlsxwriter covers the same role in Python.

native.name: py_mini_racer
native.role: JavaScript engine (V8) for V8
native.why: The R V8 package wraps V8; py_mini_racer embeds V8 in Python.

native.name: Pillow
native.role: JPEG image reading and writing for jpeg
native.why: jpeg reads and writes JPEG; Pillow covers the same role in Python.

native.name: SQLAlchemy
native.role: Database connections (Routing: DBI and withr with_db_connection)
native.why: Database connections are SQLAlchemy by the Routing rule.

native.name: pyo3
native.role: Rust-to-Python binding for the crates in crates/ (built with maturin)
native.why: Every Rust crate exposes its kernels to Python through pyo3; agreed by the user.

native.name: libblas
native.role: BLAS dnrm2, ddot and daxpy (OpenBLAS 0.3.29) called by the dqrdc2 kernel in crates/nlmegls
native.why: R's dqrdc2 calls these BLAS routines from the system library, so reproducing R's bits needs the same library. The nlme glsApVar path matches R with max abs diff 0 once dnrm2, ddot and daxpy call it through FFI (R 3.97 ms, Python 1.80 ms). Checked against nlme glsApVar and a dqrdc2 proof over 150 random cases.

native.name: PORT
native.role: nlminb optimizer routines (drmnf, drmng, drmnfb, drmnh and helpers) vendored from R 4.5.0 src/library/stats/src/portsrc.f (netlib PORT), built with gfortran in crates/nlminb_port
native.why: R's nlminb (used by nlme lme, lmeOpt, and gls) runs the PORT library. A Python optimizer cannot reproduce its step sequence, so lme and glmmPQL cannot match R to 1e-8 without it. Agreed by the user on 2026-10-17 (AskQuestion: vendor PORT).

native.name: cairosvg
native.role: SVG to PNG rendering for fontawesome fa_png
native.why: Agreed by the user. The R package rsvg is not in the registry and is not created; cairosvg renders the same SVG to PNG through cairo.
